title: Formalisme algébrique des correspondances et algèbres de Poincaré-Hodge (cf conjectures standard) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), lettres (1966-1967).

deep.reconstruction:
This page does not belong to the surrounding manuscript. The neighbouring pages contain Grothendieck's handwritten lemma that algebraicity of the Lefschetz operators implies the Künneth/Lefschetz projectors are algebraic (standard conjectures). This page is instead a typed Bourbaki document, headed 'Tribu n° 65', 'Algèbres étales et la différente (4)'. It is a set of editorial instructions for redrafting a chapter of Commutative Algebra on the different. It may have been written by Grothendieck or by another member; the page does not say.

Plan of §2 (Différente):

(n°1) Fitting ideals of a module M (the typescript writes 'Filting').
- Refer to D. Lazard's thesis (published as 'Autour de la platitude', 1968/69) and to the link with the content ideal.
- Fact cited: Fitt_0(M) lies between Ann(M) and a power of it. Precisely, if M has n generators, Ann(M)^n ⊂ Fitt_0(M) ⊂ Ann(M).

(n°2) Kähler different.
- For B of finite presentation over A (or merely Ω_{B/A} finitely presented), D_{B/A} := Fitt_0(Ω_{B/A}).
- Computed from a presentation B^p → B^q → Ω_{B/A} → 0 as the ideal generated by the q×q minors, i.e. the image of ∧^q u.
- Its zero locus V(D) = Supp Ω_{B/A} is the ramified (non-unramified) locus.
- Compatibility with base change is immediate, because Fitting ideals and Ω commute with base change.

(n°3) Transitivity.
- D_{C/A} = D_{C/B}·D_{B/A}C holds for A → B → C when C is a local complete intersection over B.

(n°4) Link with the trace.
- Define the Dedekind different as the inverse of the trace-dual (codifferent).
- Show it equals the Kähler different for an extension of DVRs, using the draft's 'gros th. 3, n°7, §2' and its dévissage through complete intersections.
- Note that a map between regular rings is a relative complete intersection.
- Prop. 11 of the draft is to be explained by a monogenicity lemma: if k → R is finite and R/rad R is étale, then R is monogenic iff its maximal ideals are 'homogènes' (surely meant: principal/monogenic). This underlies the classical fact O_L = O_K[x] when the residue extension is separable.

(n°5) Compléments.
- Tame ramification.
- The Kummer description of totally, tamely ramified extensions of a complete DVF: adjoin an n-th root of a suitably chosen uniformizer.
- Example of Riemann surfaces, where the local Galois group has the canonical generator exp(2iπ/n).

This is all standard material, later found in Bourbaki AC, Serre's Corps locaux and Kunz's Kähler Differentials.
errors: The presentation is written A^p → A^q → Ω_A(B) → 0; it should be over B (B^p → B^q), since Ω_A(B) is a B-module and the different is an ideal of B.
'Premier idéal de Filting' with Im(∧^q u) is the 0-th Fitting ideal in modern indexing. This is a naming convention, not a mathematical error.
In the monogenicity lemma, 'homogènes' must be a slip for 'monogènes/principaux'.
As stated, the monogenicity lemma needs a hypothesis when k is finite. Example: k = F_2, R = F_2^3 has principal maximal ideals and étale R/rad R, but R is not monogenic over F_2.

missed.claim: Archival note: a Bourbaki 'Tribu n° 65' plan page on étale algebras and the different is filed inside cote 16, in the middle of Grothendieck's handwritten lemma on the standard conjectures. This is useful provenance information for historians of Bourbaki's Commutative Algebra; the mathematics itself is not new.
missed.quote: Algèbres étales et la différente (4)    Tribu n° 65
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents the editorial genesis of Bourbaki's treatment of the different via Fitting ideals and the Kähler different, and possibly Grothendieck's involvement in it.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a misfiled Bourbaki editorial plan containing only standard commutative algebra (Fitting ideals, Kähler and Dedekind differents, tame ramification). It is of mild historical interest only.
transcription_corrections: 'Filting' in the original is a typo for 'Fitting'.
The presentation should read B^p → B^q → Ω_A(B) → 0; the typescript has A^p, A^q.
'idéaux maximaux de R sont homogènes' is likely intended as 'monogènes' (principal).
